mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real GDP growth above 3% for two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDP growth exceeds 3% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% and remains there for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in the industrial production index for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending proxy (RSAFS) where PAYEMS growth outpaces RSAFS growth by more than 1 percentage point for two consecutive months signals under-spending relative to income, which typically precedes fiscal stimulus and policy easing, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth exceeds RSAFS growth by >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth exceeds RSAFS growth by more than 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) move in opposite directions for three consecutive months, it indicates a disconnect between monetary policy stance and inflation dynamics, which historically precedes regime shifts and volatility spikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL move in opposite directions for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during months when FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL move in opposite directions for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months signals a significant labor market weakening, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 7% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 7% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average.
